blocks.text: 1. Embeddings

blocks.alt: A discrete token goes through an embedding table to produce a dense vector

blocks.text: Positional Encoding, the previous topic, added position information to an existing input embedding. Embeddings take a closer look at how raw input tokens become the vectors Attention operates on, explored throughout this topic.
They convert discrete tokens, like words, into genuinely continuous, learnable numeric vectors, a genuinely essential, foundational step covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Missing Piece
This connects back to added, not concatenated, already covered in Positional Encoding. Positional Encoding, already covered there, genuinely gets added to an existing input embedding.
This topic genuinely explains exactly where that embedding itself actually comes from, closing the exact gap already implicitly left open at the end of the previous topic.
3. The Discrete Tokens Challenge

blocks.alt: Discrete tokens have no inherent numeric meaning

blocks.text: This connects back to encoding sequence elements as numbers, already covered in Sequence Data. Words, or other discrete tokens, genuinely cannot be fed directly into a neural network, already covered there in general terms.
This is a genuinely real, practical challenge that Embeddings exist specifically to solve, giving that earlier general observation a genuinely concrete, working solution.

blocks.text: 4. The Core Idea

blocks.alt: Each token maps to a learned vector

blocks.text: Embeddings' genuinely core idea connects back to learned projections, already covered in Query, Key, and Value. Map each genuinely discrete token to its own genuinely learned, continuous vector.
This directly reuses the "genuinely learned" philosophy already covered there, applied here to converting discrete tokens into the continuous representations Attention actually needs.
5. The Embedding Table Lookup

blocks.alt: A token ID is looked up in the embedding table to produce a vector

blocks.text: This connects back to filters being genuinely learned, already covered in Filters and Kernels. A genuinely large table stores one learnable vector for every single possible token in the vocabulary.

Looking up a token's own embedding is genuinely just a simple, direct table lookup, a genuinely efficient, straightforward operation despite the genuinely large number of learnable parameters this table can contain.
6. Semantic Structure Genuinely Emerges

blocks.alt: Similar words end up with nearby vectors

blocks.text: This connects back to context-aware representations, already covered in Self-Attention. Through training, genuinely similar words often genuinely end up with genuinely similar embedding vectors.
This is a genuinely fascinating, real, emergent property rather than something explicitly programmed, arising naturally as the network learns to solve its own training task well.

blocks.text: 7. Choosing The Embedding Dimension

blocks.alt: A small dimension is compared against a large dimension

blocks.text: A genuinely important hyperparameter connects back to Hyperparameters, already covered in its own module. The genuinely embedding dimension controls how genuinely rich each token's own representation can be.
This is a genuinely real, tunable choice, following the exact same hyperparameter-tuning philosophy already covered generally throughout that earlier module.
8. Scaling Before Adding Positional Encoding
This connects back to Positional Encoding, already covered in the previous topic. Embeddings genuinely often get scaled before Positional Encoding, already covered there, gets added on top.

This keeps the two genuinely different sources of information at a genuinely comparable, balanced magnitude, a genuinely practical detail ensuring neither source dominates the combined representation unfairly.

blocks.text: 9. Sharing Embeddings Across Tasks

A genuinely practical, real technique connects forward to Transfer Learning, covered later in this course. Pre-trained embeddings, already covered generally, can often genuinely transfer to entirely new, different tasks.

This genuinely real, practical technique, already covered in this section, avoids needing to genuinely relearn embeddings entirely from scratch for every genuinely new task, a theme explored in complete depth later in this course.
10. Recognizing Why Embeddings Are Genuinely Essential

blocks.alt: Feeding tokens to a neural network points toward using embeddings

blocks.text: This connects back to any Transformer, already covered throughout this module, needing genuinely continuous input. Embeddings, already covered in this topic, directly provide that genuinely necessary continuous representation.
This connects forward to Word Embeddings and other embedding types, covered later in this course. Understanding this general concept now, already covered, is genuinely essential preparation.
11. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simple embedding table lookup, converting a sequence of tokens into their own learned vector representations, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
vocabulary_size = 10
embedding_dimension = 4  # already covered as the embedding dimension choice in this topic

# already covered as the embedding table lookup in this topic
embedding_table = rng.normal(size=(vocabulary_size, embedding_dimension)) * 0.1

vocabulary = {"the": 0, "cat": 1, "sat": 2, "on": 3, "mat": 4}
sentence = ["the", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
token_ids = [vocabulary[word] for word in sentence]

embedded_sequence = embedding_table[token_ids]  # already covered as the core idea in this topic

print(f"Token IDs: {token_ids}")
print(f"Embedded sequence shape: {embedded_sequence.shape}")
print(f"Embedding for 'the' (token 0): {np.round(embedding_table[0], 3)}")
print(f"Embedding for 'cat' (token 1): {np.round(embedding_table[1], 3)}")
print("\nEach genuinely discrete token became its own genuinely learned, continuous vector, already covered in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows each token mapped to its own genuinely continuous vector through a simple table lookup, exactly the core mechanism already covered in this topic as the foundation for everything that follows in the Transformer.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Embeddings convert discrete tokens into continuous, learnable numeric vectors.
Words or other discrete tokens cannot be fed directly into a neural network.
Each token maps to its own genuinely learned, continuous vector.
An embedding table stores one learnable vector per vocabulary token, accessed by simple lookup.
Through training, similar words often end up with similar embedding vectors.
The embedding dimension is a tunable hyperparameter controlling representational richness.
Embeddings often get scaled before Positional Encoding gets added on top.
Pre-trained embeddings can often transfer to entirely new, different tasks.
